report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Render eval results as ASCII tables with provenance and focus-withheld honesty notes.

symbols.name: _PROVENANCE_NOTE
symbols.note: Per-provenance honesty notes; hand_reachable is self-graded.

symbols.name: _rule
symbols.note: Builds a horizontal rule using + and -.

symbols.name: _row
symbols.note: Builds a table row with left-justified cells.

symbols.name: _focus_withheld_lines
symbols.note: Returns focus-withheld bucket lines; empty if none.

symbols.name: _table
symbols.note: Builds a full ASCII table with header and rows.

symbols.name: _pct
symbols.note: Formats a fraction as a percentage with one decimal.

symbols.name: _provenance_breakdown_lines
symbols.note: Renders provenance breakdown with per-provenance notes.

symbols.name: render_tier1
symbols.note: Renders Tier 1 recall/compression report with missed/errored sections.

symbols.name: render_arms
symbols.note: Renders A/B/C arms report with truncation and tie/beat blocks.

claims.text: No unicode box-drawing, no fancy glyphs: only + - |
claims.why: All table-building uses only '+', '-', '|' and spaces; no other glyphs appear.

claims.text: Framing is honest: this is a small private directional eval
claims.why: The module's purpose is stated but the 'private directional' nature cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: recall is necessary-not-sufficient
claims.why: render_tier1 explains recall as 'necessary, not sufficient -- proves no load-bearing context was dropped'.

claims.text: Tier 2 needs a runtime
claims.why: The module does not mention Tier 2 runtime requirements; that claim is outside this file.

claims.text: "hand_reachable" recall is partly self-graded and MUST NOT be blended with independently-derived recall into one headline number.
claims.why: _provenance_breakdown_lines prints per-provenance rows and the header 'never blended -- this is the honest number'; no blending is performed.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD (lane A1) -- honest, ASCII-only accounting for tasks where the unconditional secret floor fail-closed on the task's OWN focus file
claims.why: The docstring references harness._is_focus_withheld and slice.py's FOCUS GATE, which are not in this chunk; the mechanism cannot be verified.

claims.text: Neither a pass (no slice text was ever compared to must_include) nor a recall miss (the label was never even attempted) -- its own bucket, excluded from every mean/count above.
claims.why: The function returns lines that explicitly state 'EXCLUDED from every mean/count above'; it is a separate bucket.

claims.text: Absent (result.get) for any hand-built result dict that predates this field, and adds no lines when there are none.
claims.why: Uses result.get('focus_withheld_ids') or [] and returns [] if empty; adds no lines when none.

claims.text: Shared renderer for the 'PROVENANCE BREAKDOWN' block used by both Tier 1 and the arms report.
claims.why: Both render_tier1 and render_arms call _provenance_breakdown_lines.

claims.text: Always shows both tiers (even when empty) and always prints the honesty note
claims.why: For each provenance, the note is printed unconditionally; both primary and quarantine tiers are iterated, though rows are only added when n_tasks != 0.

claims.text: this block is the deliverable of this sprint
claims.why: Sprint scoping is a project-management claim outside the code.

claims.text: Errored rows carry no recall/compression/slice_tokens/... at all (see harness._task_error_row) -- they get their own ERRORED section below, not a row in this recall/compression table.
claims.why: The comment references harness._task_error_row, which is not in this chunk; the absence of fields cannot be verified here.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD rows (see harness._focus_withheld_row) are excluded the same way, into their own section below.
claims.why: References harness._focus_withheld_row, not present in this chunk; the exclusion logic itself is visible (skips t.get('focus_withheld')).

claims.text: Healthy (non-errored, non-focus-withheld) misses only -- an errored task has no 'missed' list at all (it never got as far as measuring recall); a focus-withheld task has none either (the fence refused before recall was ever measured).
claims.why: The claim about why errored/focus-withheld tasks have no 'missed' list depends on harness behavior not visible here; the filter itself is correct.

claims.text: Both are reported in their own unmissable sections, not folded in here as a miss.
claims.why: Errored tasks go to the ERRORED section; focus-withheld tasks go to _focus_withheld_lines; misses filter excludes both.

claims.text: ERORRED section -- a per-task resolution failure (bad repo label, or a target no longer in the index -- e.g. a quarantined mint task whose file moved) is EXCLUDED from every mean above but must never go unreported: 'a degraded measurement is reported, never silent.'
claims.why: The reasons for errored tasks are described but not verifiable from this code; the exclusion from means is visible in the filter.

claims.text: Absent entirely (result.get, not result[...]) for any pre-existing caller that hand-built a Tier-1 result dict without this key -- and always absent when there are zero errored tasks, so this block adds NO lines to that report.
claims.why: Uses result.get('errored') or [] and only appends lines if non-empty.

claims.text: A/B/C: distilled slice vs whole-repo concat vs BM25 retrieval. Model-free (recall via substring match, no LLM), so this runs offline every time.
claims.why: The claim that recall is via substring match and no LLM is not verifiable from this rendering code; it depends on the data.

claims.text: Errored rows carry no recall_A/tokens_A/... at all (see harness._task_error_row) -- they are reported in their own section below, not in this table.
claims.why: References harness._task_error_row; the data absence cannot be verified here.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD rows (harness._focus_withheld_row) are excluded the same way, into their own section.
claims.why: References harness._focus_withheld_row; the exclusion itself is visible in the healthy filter.

claims.text: B_TRUNC@CAP = yes means: if this task ran Tier 2, B would be cut down to fit the model's context window -- a WEAKER baseline than the R_B/TOK_B shown here.
claims.why: The comment explains the meaning of b_truncated_at_cap; the rendering uses it directly.

claims.text: C = BM25 (k1=1.2, b=0.75) top-k retrieval, budgeted to the SAME token count as A.
claims.why: The BM25 parameters and budgeting are not in this chunk; only the rendering is.

claims.text: c_beats_a is tie-inclusive (recall_C >= recall_A, see harness.eval_task_arms)
claims.why: References harness.eval_task_arms; the tie-inclusive semantics cannot be verified here.

claims.text: A tie ('BM25 matches the product's recall at equal cost') is the commercially damning case, not merely a strict loss for A.
claims.why: The comment states this and the code reports ties loudly in the beats block.

claims.text: B WOULD BE TRUNCATED for {len(trunc)}/{len(healthy)} tasks if run through Tier 2 (context-window cap) -- the R_B/TOK_B columns above are the TRUE untruncated baseline, not what a live LLM run would see
claims.why: The code prints the true tokens_B and capped tokens_B, and the comment explains the distinction.

claims.text: ERORRED section -- same rationale as render_tier1's: excluded from every arm/aggregate above, never silently dropped. Absent when there are none.
claims.why: Uses result.get('errored') or [] and only appends if non-empty; the exclusion is visible in the healthy filter.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD rows are excluded from every mean/count above
claims.why: The function returns lines stating 'EXCLUDED from every mean/count above'; the filters in render_tier1 and render_arms skip focus_withheld tasks.

claims.text: Errored rows are excluded from every recall/compression figure above
claims.why: The filter skips tasks with 'error' in t.

claims.text: Errored rows are excluded from every arm/aggregate above
claims.why: The healthy filter skips tasks with 'error' in t.

observations.what: The healthy filter in render_arms uses t.get('focus_withheld') to exclude focus-withheld tasks, but the comment says they are excluded 'into their own section'; _focus_withheld_lines is called, so the section is present.

The _provenance_breakdown_lines function iterates over sorted(by_provenance) and for each provenance prints a note and then iterates tiers; if a provenance has no tiers with n_tasks > 0, the note is still printed but no rows are added. The docstring says 'Always shows both tiers (even when empty)' which is true in the sense that the tier loop is always executed, but empty tiers produce no visible rows.
The comment in render_tier1 says 'a focus-withheld task has none either (the fence refused before recall was ever measured)' but this is a claim about harness behavior not verifiable in this chunk.

The comment in render_arms says 'c_beats_a is tie-inclusive (recall_C >= recall_A, see harness.eval_task_arms)' but the rendering code only checks t['c_beats_a']; the tie-inclusive semantics are not verifiable here.
The comment in render_arms says 'C = BM25 (k1=1.2, b=0.75) top-k retrieval, budgeted to the SAME token count as A' but no BM25 parameters or budgeting logic is present in this chunk.

risks: render_arms | low | The healthy filter excludes focus_withheld tasks, but the comment says they are excluded 'into their own section'; verify that _focus_withheld_lines is always called and prints correctly when there are focus_withheld tasks. | Check that _focus_withheld_lines is called unconditionally in render_arms and that it handles empty ids.

render_arms | low | The comment claims c_beats_a is tie-inclusive, but the code only checks the boolean; if the harness sets c_beats_a to false on ties, the comment would be wrong. | Inspect harness.eval_task_arms to confirm the tie-inclusive semantics.
